trust_decision.summary: A hook file path built from a user-supplied name, or discovered inside a hook directory, must resolve inside the hook directory and must not be a symlink; at the pinned commit nothing makes that decision - the name is concatenated unchecked in `hooks remove` (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:146-165), `hooks edit` (:203-223) and `hooks test` (:341-353), and the shared directory enumerator accepts any entry including symlinks (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:425-426), which `runHook` then executes (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:441).

landing_point.why: A reader told only 'Path Traversal in Hook Files - Directory Escape' opens the hooks command file and finds the one interactive command where a user string becomes a hook path: `hookFileName := args[0]` joined at cmd/uniget/hooks.go:210, run through $EDITOR at :227 and chmod'd at :236. remove (:146) and test (:341) are the neighbouring same-shaped joins.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: cmd/uniget/hooks.go:407-433 (processHooks) - the fix changes this shared enumerator, which is reached from cmd/uniget/install.go:266 and cmd/uniget/uninstall.go:48, i.e. outside the hooks subcommand surface the advisory summary names

O3_reason_to_dismiss: processHooks is the internal directory walker used by install/uninstall; a solver reads the report as 'the hooks subcommands accept ../ names', fixes remove and edit, and argues the install-time enumerator only ever sees entries the CLI itself listed, so it needs no symlink guard - leaving every install/uninstall hook run unguarded.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ordinary hook scripts must keep working, and an editor may carry its own arguments. The published fix guards symlinks with `if err == nil { return ... 'is a symlink' }` on os.Lstat, which is true for every existing regular file, so `hooks list`, `hooks run` and `hooks edit` would reject all real hooks; collapsing UNIGET_EDITOR/EDITOR to its first token also drops legitimate flags such as `code --wait`.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: cmd/uniget/hooks_test.go:41-47 (TestProcessHooks expects a regular test.sh to be processed and run) with cmd/uniget/hooks.go:421-423 (the existing and sufficient skip rules: directories and dot-prefixed entries)

O6_input_shapes: relative traversal inside the name argument (`../../..` components) on `hooks remove` and `hooks edit`, normalised by filepath.Abs and rejected by the prefix check
a plain hook name that must stay accepted (the same code path)
a symlink entry discovered while walking a hook directory (processHooks), rejected by the added os.Lstat test
an EDITOR / UNIGET_EDITOR value containing spaces and extra tokens, reduced to its first token and passed hookFile as a single argv element

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `uniget hooks test <name> [args...]` joins the user-supplied args[0] into the hook path and execs it, so a name that escapes the hook directory runs any executable on the host - the most severe sink in the file and the only hook route the published fix did not touch
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: 'test' is a developer convenience command outside the install/uninstall hook pipeline, and it only runs a file the operator explicitly named, so it looks like an intentional escape hatch rather than the vulnerability
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and same package as the landing point (cmd/uniget/hooks.go), reached through runHook at :355 and :441

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `uniget hooks add --source <path>` writes its destination through os.Create (pkg/os/io.go:123), which follows a symlink already present in the hook directory, so the write escapes the hook dir even though the name is only the source basename; the fix adds no symlink guard on this write path while it adds one to edit and processHooks
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the destination name is derived from the source basename so it cannot traverse, and the hook directory is root-owned, so the route needs a symlink somebody else already placed
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: cmd/uniget/hooks.go:96-118 into the pkg/os helper (pkg/os/io.go:114-137), one package away from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-name variant such as `hooks run --hook <name>` or `hooks show <name>` built with the same `hookDir + "/" + name` concatenation that testHookCmd already uses
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the CLI already has per-type commands and one per-name command (test); running or printing a single named hook is the obvious next feature and the maintainer would copy the existing concatenation from :346

O8b_injection_room.sibling: `hooks restore` / `hooks import` that recreates a saved hook set (name+type pairs from a manifest file on disk), i.e. a config-loader-shaped producer feeding the same join
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the CLI already has an `import` command that reconciles on-disk state into managed metadata (cmd/uniget/import.go:16-40) while hooks are the only operator state with no import or restore path, so a manifest-driven hook restore is a natural addition whose names would not come from an operator's argv

O8b_injection_room.sibling: `hooks disable` / `hooks enable` that renames a named hook to a dot-prefixed name, taking the name from argv and calling os.Rename inside the hook dir
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: processHooks already skips dot-prefixed entries (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:421-423), so disable-by-rename is a one-line feature the maintainer would add next to runHooks, and it would need the same containment check

O9_family: path traversal / arbitrary file access and execution through user-controlled paths (CWE-22, CWE-23, CWE-36, CWE-73)

O10_build.project_tests: cmd/uniget/hooks_test.go:9-28 TestRunHook and :30-52 TestProcessHooks drive runHook/processHooks with local shell scripts (bash on PATH); the cobra end-to-end harness is runCobraTest at cmd/uniget/main_test.go:27-47. The fix diff adds or changes no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Abs(hookFile), hooksDir)` to `hooks edit` and `hooks remove` only, with the symlink test written as `if err == nil`, leaving `hooks test`, the `hooks add` write path and symlink-following os.Create open while rejecting every real hook file.
